text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.93% today to $130.61, continuing a three-day slide from its peak of $134.89 on August 20th. The decline tracks the broader oil market weakness over the past few days—crude dropped more than 3% on August 25th as the U.S. shifted away from military confrontation with Iran toward economic pressure instead, easing immediate concerns about supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. As negotiations between Iran and Oman progress on joint administration of that crucial shipping corridor, market anxiety about geopolitical conflict in the region has cooled, taking some of the risk premium out of oil prices.

The stock has still gained 2.6% over two weeks, so today's pullback is a modest retreat from recent highs rather than a reversal of the broader trend. The easing of war fears removes one of the factors that had supported energy prices earlier this month.
